newsitem.title: UK: UK jobless can fall without inflation threat - CEBR.
newsitem.headline: UK jobless can fall without inflation threat - CEBR.

text.p: The number of jobless in Britain could fall by another 500,000 without fuelling inflationary pressures, economic consultancy the Centre for Economics and Business Research said on Wednesday.

Professor Douglas McWilliams, chief executive of the CEBR, said the unemployment rate could fall to five percent from 6.9 now but added that unemployment was currently falling at a "dangerously fast" rate.
He said jobless queues were currently being cut by about 40,000 people a month.

"This is too rapid. If unemployment continued to fall at this pace it would lead to inflationary pressures and to higher interest rates, which would in turn eventually bring the falls in unemployment to an end."

He said a sustainable pace of decline would see the jobless total fall by 10,000 a month. "This would be a pace of decline that would be consistent with inflation staying low and hence with a sustained reduction in unemployment," he said.

Official unemployment figures are due out at 0930 GMT on Wednesday. A Reuter poll of economists found a consensus forecast that Britain's jobless queues were reduced by 30,000 last month, following a record drop of 96,000 the month before.
McWilliams said the increase in labour market flexibility, arising from the reforms carried out in the 1980s and 1990s, made falls in unemployment more likely.
